topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: Introduces the cancer lecture series and outlines the key learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Cancer Evolution, Endogenous Mutagenesis, and Genetic Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: Establishes how cancer develops as a clonal evolutionary process driven by intrinsic cellular errors, replication stress, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Carcinogens, Epidemiological Variation, and Risk Perception
topics.groupedBecause: Explores population-level epidemiological patterns and the public debate surrounding extrinsic environmental exposures versus stochastic cancer risk.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Pathogen, Chemical, and Physical Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: Details the biological and biochemical mechanisms through which specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents act as tumor initiators or promoters.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: Surveys the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to identify mutational signatures and test carcinogen potency.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Carcinogen Risk-Benefit Evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: Concludes the lecture by reviewing the challenges of assessing carcinogen potency and framing environmental exposure within risk-benefit decisions.
